minutes.headline: Water Commissioners tabled a vote on new well testing, deferring it to a future special meeting
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners approved paying a Tighe & Bond engineering invoice and reviewed results of exploratory test wells near the Keing well site, but tabled a decision on further well investment until a special meeting can be called for public input. They also discussed Neptune meter-reading upgrades, a DEP non-compliance notice on PFAS sampling, hiring an additional operator, upcoming commissioner elections, and revisions to a resident survey comparing well-source options and their loan costs.

what_happened.line: Commissioners tabled a vote on further test-well investment near the Keing site, deferring it to a special meeting for public input.
The board voted to let Fran pay the Tighe & Bond engineering invoice, the amount as heard in captions, from the maintenance budget.
Commissioners agreed to move forward with hiring an additional water treatment operator using already-budgeted funds.
The district discussed adding Neptune meter-reading data collectors on both water tanks and a possible antenna site near Hickory Hills as a special-meeting budget item.
The district reported a DEP non-compliance notice over required monthly PFAS sampling at the Lancaster wells.

why_it_matters: Tabling the well-testing vote means residents get a public hearing before the district commits further money toward a new well source versus a future PFAS treatment plant, either of which could affect water rates or a loan.
